LanguageData.M3AT_DefaultsRestored: M3AT's options are back to their defaults.
LanguageData.M3AT_PawnSizeTip: How tall a grown pawn is drawn, in map cells; the percentage is against the mod's usual height (100%, the default). Children, gender and height variety are on top of it. It changes only how pawns look, not the space they take up.
LanguageData.M3AT_HeadShrinkTip: How much smaller the head is drawn than the default chibi. Left: default; right: smaller. No effect on vanilla or CE hit calculations.
LanguageData.M3AT_HeightVarietyTip: How much pawns' heights vary (default {0}). A normal distribution is used, with most near the usual size and a few further off. 0% makes everyone of a gender the same size. Each pawn's height is derived from the pawn's id, so no save data is needed.
LanguageData.M3AT_GenderSizesTip: Renders men and women with a 10% size difference eased in over teenage years. Off: they are the same size.
LanguageData.M3AT_SkeletonsTip: Corpses dried to bones and the shamblers raised from them are drawn as a cartoon skeleton in the chibi's proportions, moving as the chibi does, in whatever they still wear. Off: IsoRim's own skeleton.
LanguageData.M3AT_AgingLooksTip: Older pawns get wrinkles in stages from their late forties, a stooped back from their late fifties (more with a bad back or frailty) and lose a little height; cataracts cloud the eye. Ages go by each race's life expectancy. Off: old pawns look young.
LanguageData.M3AT_GreyingHairTip: Hair fades to grey as pawns grow old, from where the game left it, so a pawn made dark-haired stays so until it ages further. A dye or other new hair colour shows as chosen and only greys again with more age. Pawns with genes that keep their hair from greying never grey. Only the drawing changes: the pawn's own hair colour is untouched.
LanguageData.M3AT_OtherRacesTip: Pawns of modded races (Ratkin, Milira and the like) are drawn as animated 3D pawns rather than flat pictures, unless an IsoRim pack already gives the race a 3D look. They get the race's skin colour, hair, clothes and face, and with the option below its ears, tails and the like. IsoRim's "Keep as paper" list still keeps any race flat.
LanguageData.M3AT_RacePartsTip: A modded race's ears, tails, horns, wings and the like are made into 3D shapes from the race's own pictures, so the race keeps its look on 3D pawns. They are rough stand-ins: a part that is thin in life may come out thick.
LanguageData.M3AT_RaceMouthInkTip: Soft, painted mouths (Facial Animation - Experimentals' own and modded races') are redrawn with dark outlines and without their pale glow and lip shading, so they read on the large 3D face. Faces already drawn with hard lines, such as Facial Animation - Retexture's, keep their lines.
LanguageData.M3AT_MouthSizeFitTip: A modded race's mouths are drawn at about a human's size, and any mouth shape much wider than usual is drawn narrower, in proportion to how much too wide it is. Turn it off to draw every mouth at the size its face mod draws it.
LanguageData.M3AT_SharpFaceArtTip: Facial Animation's eyes, brows and mouths (and those of face mods for other races) are drawn sharper on the 3D face: a little crisper from the usual camera, and in close-ups their soft, blurred edges are redrawn as clean lines. Turn it off to see the art exactly as the face mod draws it.
LanguageData.M3AT_BodyShapeStrengthTip: How strongly thin, fat and hulk bodies are shaped (default 100%). Lower makes them closer to an average build, higher exaggerates them; past 100% clothes may clip into the body. Also scales the builds from Varied bodies. Male and female shapes are unchanged.
LanguageData.M3AT_VariedBodiesTip: Each pawn gets a build of its own, somewhere around its body type: some thinner or heavier, some more muscular, so not every average body looks the same. Thin, fat and hulk pawns are still based on those bodies. Off: every pawn of a body type has the same body.
LanguageData.M3AT_BodyVarietyTip: How far pawns' builds wander from their body type (default {0}). Most stay near it, a few go most of the way to the next type. Each pawn's build is derived from the pawn's id, so no save data is needed.
LanguageData.M3AT_HairDetailTip: How much of the shape of each hairstyle made from its sprites is kept (default {0}). Higher looks smoother and follows the art more closely, but costs more with many pawns on screen. Hair a mod supplies as a 3D model is always drawn in full. Takes effect when this window closes.
LanguageData.M3AT_BeardsTip:
2D (default): the beard's sprite is laid flat on the face. Cheap, but only seen from the front, and cut off at the chin.

3D: each beard is built as a 3D mesh from its sprites the first time it is worn, so it is seen from every side.

Off: no beards are drawn or built.
LanguageData.M3AT_EyeMovementTip: How far pawns' eyes glance and look about with Facial Animation, against how far they move on its 2D faces (default {0}). Its movements are small, a pixel or so, so higher makes them easier to see on the bigger 3D faces. 0%: the eyes stay still. Brows, eyelids and mouths move as Facial Animation moves them, whatever this is.
LanguageData.M3AT_TalkingMouthsTip: With Facial Animation, a pawn's mouth opens and shuts as it talks: chatting with someone, at a party, visiting a patient, giving a speech. Uses each face's own open mouth. Off: mouths only move as Facial Animation moves them.
LanguageData.M3AT_ShoesTip: A pawn whose clothes cover both the body and the legs (a shirt and trousers, or a duster, robe or suit) has plain shoes on. Off: bare feet unless a mod's shoes are worn.
LanguageData.M3AT_ArmourHidesTailTip: A pawn with a tail gene wearing full body armour (power, recon, cataphract or plate armour) has its tail hidden, as it would otherwise go through the armour. Vacsuits leave it out. Off: the tail is always shown.
LanguageData.M3AT_EarHidingTip:
Whether cat, pig or floppy ears are hidden under what a pawn wears on its head, as they would otherwise go through it.

Any headgear (default): helmets, and hats that cover the top of the head.

Helmets only: armour helmets (simple, advanced, power armour, recon, cataphract and the like); the ears poke through other hats.

Never: the ears are always shown.
LanguageData.M3AT_WornGearTip: Jump packs, shield belts and the other packs, belts and lances a pawn wears are shown on its back or waist, and headsets, masks, crowns, blindfolds and slave collars on its head and neck, with IsoRim's models of them. Off: they are not shown.
LanguageData.M3AT_SpriteClothes: Paint stand-in clothes with their own art
LanguageData.M3AT_SpriteClothesTip: Clothes from other mods that have no 3D garment of their own are drawn as the nearest one M3AT has (a dress, a skirt, a jacket). With this on, that garment is painted with the clothing's own sprites, front, sides and back, so it keeps its colours, trim and patterns. Off: the garment's plain texture in the clothing's colour.
LanguageData.M3AT_GroundGarmentsTip: Clothes on the map will be drawn as the same 3D garment a pawn wears, squashed flat. Off (default): IsoRim's 3D models are used. Takes effect when this window closes.
LanguageData.M3AT_BedBlanketsTip: In beds that show only the sleeper's head, IsoRim's blanket is drawn over the body, raised by it. Other beds, such as sleeping spots and bedrolls, have no blanket. Off (default): pawns lie on top of every bed.
LanguageData.M3AT_HelmetStowTip:
How colonists' armour helmets are shown. Only how they look: the helmet stays worn in the game and still protects.

Always worn (default): always on the head.

On the back when undrafted: taken off when undrafted and carried on the back, a little smaller; put back on when drafted.

Hidden when undrafted: not drawn while undrafted, with no animation.

Always hidden: never drawn, drafted or not.
LanguageData.M3AT_SleepWearTip:
What pawns lying in a bed are drawn wearing, wherever their body shows (a bed with no blanket, or with blankets off). Only how they look: nothing is taken off or put on in the game.

Normal clothes: what they wear.

No equipment (default): without armour, helmets and hats, coats, belts, packs or shields; shirts, trousers and the like stay on.

Pajamas: pastel pajamas; babies in their romper.

No clothes: no clothes; babies keep their romper.
LanguageData.M3AT_VatClothesTip: Pawns in growth vats and biosculpter pods are drawn in their clothes. Off (default): they are drawn without them. Babies never get their romper in a vat.
LanguageData.M3AT_InjuryAnimsTip: Pawns limp on a bad leg, hold injured areas, etc. Off: they move as if unhurt. Off doesn't disable hit flinch animations, hopping for missing legs, or slowed movement.
LanguageData.M3AT_VisibleWoundsTip: Wounds, blood, bandages and scars are drawn on the pawn, where the injury is. Wounds and blood are visible through some clothing; bruises, bandages and scars go only on the skin. Off: none are drawn.
LanguageData.M3AT_ProstheticsTip: Peg legs, wooden hands and feet, and simple, bionic and archotech arms and legs are drawn as what they are made of, where clothes leave them bare. Off: a replaced limb looks like skin.
LanguageData.M3AT_ProstheticEyesTip: Bionic and archotech eyes are drawn with a mechanical iris. Off: they look like the pawn's own eyes.
LanguageData.M3AT_ArchotechProstheticsTip: Archotech limbs are drawn in the olive and yellow-circuit look of archotech machinery. Off: they look like natural flesh, as the game used to describe them.
LanguageData.M3AT_OutlinesHeaderTip: Click to show or hide the outline and its style.
LanguageData.M3AT_OutlinesTip: Pawns are drawn with a dark outline round the body, clothes and hair, as IsoRim draws its models. Off: no outline. Weapons and tools keep IsoRim's own.
LanguageData.M3AT_OutlineModeTip: Silhouette: the outline goes only round the outside of the pawn, never over its own body. Lines over the body: as IsoRim draws its outlines, with lines over the body too where a part such as an arm is well in front of the rest. Screen-space: the outline is found on screen from the edges of each part, so it also goes round thin and open parts such as shoulder pads, and round a held weapon in front of the body, with its own width for pawns and weapons. Screen-space needs IsoRim's scene depth; in IsoRim's photos it is drawn as the silhouette.
LanguageData.M3AT_PawnOutlineWidthTip: How wide the screen-space outline round a pawn is, in hundredths of a cell, so it is thinner when zoomed out. Close up it stops growing at the close-up width limit below. Default: {0}.
LanguageData.M3AT_WeaponOutlineWidthTip: How wide the screen-space outline round a held weapon is, and between a weapon and the hands or body holding it, in hundredths of a cell. Close up it stops growing at the close-up width limit below. Default: {0}.
LanguageData.M3AT_SelfOutlinesTip: Screen-space outlines also over the pawn's own body, where a part such as an arm or a hand is well in front of the rest. Off: only round the outside of the pawn and between it and what it holds.
LanguageData.M3AT_SelfOutlineStepTip: How far in front of the rest of the body a part must be for a line over it, in hundredths of a cell. Smaller: more lines, down to creases. Default: {0}.
LanguageData.M3AT_ScreenOutlinesUnavailable: Screen-space outlines can't be drawn this session (IsoRim can't read the scene depth, or a shader is missing), so the silhouette is drawn.
LanguageData.M3AT_FirstPersonEye: First person from the pawn's eyes
LanguageData.M3AT_FirstPersonEyeTip: IsoRim's first person looks out from where the pawn's eyes are drawn, so lower for a child and higher for a tall adult, and lower when sitting, lying or swimming. Off: IsoRim's own eye height setting is used for everyone. Needs a recent IsoRim.
LanguageData.M3AT_ClothesOcclusionTip: With IsoRim's ambient occlusion or screen-space shadows on, clothes and hair are darkened in their creases and by shadows as the rest of the world is. It picks out their flat faces, so they look less smooth. Off: pawns are left out of both, though they still cast shadows. Skin and faces are always left out, as it spoils the eyes.
LanguageData.M3AT_ClothesOcclusionStrengthTip: How much of IsoRim's ambient occlusion and screen-space shadows clothes and hair take. Lower softens the dark patches it leaves in creases and on flat faces; 100% is the same as the rest of the world.
LanguageData.M3AT_RagdollsTip: Pawns knocked down or killed where they stand fall limp under their own weight and lie as they land. Off: they play a set fall instead.
LanguageData.M3AT_FlingPowerTip: How far blows throw bodies and weapons (default 100%). 200% throws them about twice as far. With "Throw bodies" on, the biggest blasts throw a grown pawn about 6 cells at 100% and about 30 at 500%, and a grenade about a quarter of that; with it off, this only changes how hard a body is knocked about where it falls.
LanguageData.M3AT_FlingBodiesTip: Enough damage can throw the pawn they knock down or kill. Explosions and heavy melee move most. This lets M3AT move things around in the game itself, so could cause issues in multiplayer or other mods that expect the game alone to decide where things are. Off: bodies stay in the cell they fell in.
LanguageData.M3AT_FlingWeaponsTip: The weapon a pawn drops as it goes down can be flung. This lets M3AT move things around in the game itself, not only on screen, so could cause issues in multiplayer or other mods that expect the game alone to decide where things are. Off: it is dropped at the pawn's feet.
LanguageData.M3AT_HolstersTip: A weapon a pawn carries but isn't holding, and any in its inventory, is shown on its back or hip. Off: only weapons in hand are shown.
LanguageData.M3AT_MuzzleFlashTip: A gun fired by a pawn flashes at the end of its barrel, a burst of fire along the shot as well as the game's own glow. Off: only the game's glow.
LanguageData.M3AT_HitFlashTip: A pawn that takes damage flashes red for a moment, as the game's own pawns and IsoRim's 3D figures do. Off: no flash.
LanguageData.M3AT_AutoGrips: Find grips on other mods' weapons
LanguageData.M3AT_AutoGripsTip: Guns and melee weapons from other mods are held by the grip or handle found in their art, rather than where the game's own weapon of that kind is held. Where the art doesn't show a clear grip, the usual hold is kept. Off: always the usual hold.
LanguageData.M3AT_RetexturedWeaponModelsTip: The game's own weapons are shown as IsoRim's 3D models even when another mod (such as Combat Extended or a texture pack) gives them new art, or removes their models. The model is lined up with the new art but keeps its own shape, so a weapon redrawn very differently may not match it. Weapons from other mods are left to IsoRim. Off: IsoRim's choice, which shows a retextured weapon as its art. Needs IsoRim's "Weapons as 3D models" setting. Takes effect when this window closes for weapons on the ground.
LanguageData.M3AT_WeaponSizesTip: Click to show or hide each weapon type's size in the hands and on the body.
LanguageData.M3AT_WeaponSizeTip: This weapon type's size in a pawn's hands or on its body, against the same weapon lying on the ground, with "Pawn height" at 100% (default {0}). 100% here is the size IsoRim draws it on the ground. Weapons grow and shrink with "Pawn height", so this doesn't need changing when that does.
LanguageData.M3AT_SlabScaleTip: Weapons with no 3D model (most other mods' weapons, or every weapon with IsoRim's weapon models off) are drawn as a flat slab cut from their picture, which comes out longer than the 3D models. This shrinks them to match, on top of each weapon type's size above (default {0}).
LanguageData.M3AT_GpuSkinningTip: Moves each pawn's body, clothes and hair into its pose on the graphics card, which is much faster with many pawns in view. Turn it off if pawns look broken or stretched, to animate them the old way.
LanguageData.M3AT_OutlineDetailIntro: Only for the screen-space outline style. Each line is found by looking round every pixel near a pawn for a nearer part. These set how hard it looks: more is smoother lines close up but costs more frame time when a pawn fills the screen. At the usual play distance they make little difference.
LanguageData.M3AT_OutlineReachTip: The widest a line can be drawn, in pixels on a 1080-row screen (more on a taller one). Zoomed in past where the widths above reach it, the lines stay this wide, so those sliders change nothing there. Lower: thinner lines when zoomed right in, and cheaper. The Default and Faster buttons below set it too. Default: {0}.
LanguageData.M3AT_OutlineProbeDirsTip: Before the full search, a few pixels round each one are checked to see whether a line could be there at all. More points: fewer gaps at thin parts and corners, but slower. Default: {0}.
LanguageData.M3AT_OutlineProbeRingsTip: How many rings of those points, from the widest line in toward the pixel. More: catches small parts better, but slower. Default: {0}.
LanguageData.M3AT_OutlineRingsTip: The most rings the full search looks at round a pixel. More: wide lines close up have smooth edges rather than steps and notches at corners, but cost the most. Default: {0}.
LanguageData.M3AT_FewerPosesTip: When many pawns are in view they are animated less often, giving a stop-motion like effect. Reduces M3AT's performance overhead around 6–9%. Off: Pawn animated as normal. (Default)
LanguageData.M3AT_BenchmarkTip: Measures how fast the game runs with M3AT's pawns and with IsoRim's own pawns (as without this mod), on the map you are looking at. Nothing in your game is changed.
LanguageData.M3AT_BenchmarkNeedsGame: To measure the frame rate, load a game and turn on IsoRim's 3D view.
LanguageData.M3AT_BenchIntro:
This measures how fast the game runs with M3AT's pawns, with IsoRim's own pawns (as without this mod) and with no people drawn at all. It takes turns between them, so changes in the scene count against each the same.
Before you start, point the camera at your colonists the way you usually play and leave the game running at your usual speed. Don't move the camera or click anything while it measures. Nothing in your game is changed.
LanguageData.M3AT_BenchTryNone: Also measure with no people drawn
LanguageData.M3AT_BenchTryNoneTip: Adds a turn with no people drawn at all, to show how much of the frame drawing people takes with M3AT and with IsoRim.
LanguageData.M3AT_BenchTryAddOnsTip: Adds turns with the mods that add to M3AT's drawing turned off, so their cost is shown apart from M3AT's own:\n{0}
LanguageData.M3AT_BenchAddOnParts: {0} garments, {1} changes to M3AT's code, {2} poses
LanguageData.M3AT_BenchOwnCost: M3AT itself, without add-ons, costs {0} ms a frame over IsoRim's figures (noise ±{1} ms).
LanguageData.M3AT_BenchAddOnsCost: The add-ons together cost {0} ms a frame (noise ±{1} ms).
LanguageData.M3AT_BenchAddOnsSame: The add-ons together cost nothing that can be told from the noise (±{0} ms).
LanguageData.M3AT_BenchAddOnSame: {0} costs nothing that can be told from the noise (±{1} ms).
LanguageData.M3AT_BenchUnpaused: Keep the game unpaused while it measures.
LanguageData.M3AT_BenchFlicker: The pawns switch back and forth about once a second while it measures: that is the test taking turns.
LanguageData.M3AT_BenchCopied: Results copied to the clipboard. They are also saved in {0}.
LanguageData.M3AT_BenchWaitHair: Waiting for {0} hairstyles to be built first...
LanguageData.M3AT_BenchLeft: About {0} seconds left. Keep the camera still.
LanguageData.M3AT_BenchRow: {0}: {1} FPS (1% low {2} FPS), {3} ms a frame
LanguageData.M3AT_BenchCostMore: M3AT's pawns take {0} ms longer a frame than IsoRim's: {1} FPS instead of {2} ({3}% fewer).
LanguageData.M3AT_BenchCostLess: M3AT's pawns took {0} ms less a frame than IsoRim's: {1} FPS against {2}.
LanguageData.M3AT_BenchSame: M3AT's pawns and IsoRim's came out about the same ({0} ms apart, within the measuring noise of about {1} ms).
LanguageData.M3AT_BenchPeople: Drawing the people takes {0} ms a frame with M3AT and {1} ms with IsoRim, with about {2} in view: about {3} ms for each M3AT pawn.
LanguageData.M3AT_BenchFewerSaves: Switching "{0}" {1} saved {2} ms a frame ({3} FPS).
LanguageData.M3AT_BenchFewerNoSaving: Switching "{0}" {1} made no clear difference ({2} FPS).
LanguageData.M3AT_BenchNoChibis: No M3AT pawns were drawn. Were any people in view in IsoRim's 3D view?
LanguageData.M3AT_BenchFewPeople: Few people were in view. Point the camera at a group of colonists for a clearer result.
LanguageData.M3AT_BenchCapped: Drawing people made almost no difference at all. The frame rate may be held down by vsync or a frame limit, which hides the difference: turn those off to measure.
LanguageData.M3AT_BenchSpeedChanged: The game speed was changed while it measured, so the numbers are less certain.
LanguageData.M3AT_BenchStoppedView: Stopped: IsoRim's 3D view was turned off.
LanguageData.M3AT_BugReportCopied: Bug report copied to the clipboard.
LanguageData.M3AT_BugReportCopiedSaved: Bug report copied to the clipboard and saved to {0}.
LanguageData.M3AT_BugReportPaste: Paste it into the mod's bug report thread with a few words on what went wrong.
LanguageData.M3AT_BugReportNote: Copies this mod's settings, errors and your mod list for a bug report, and the state of any pawns selected in the game: select the one that looks wrong first. Nothing is sent anywhere.
LanguageData.M3AT_RestoreDefaultsConfirm: Put every M3AT option back to its default, the weapon sizes too?
LanguageData.M3AT_FreecamIntro: Fly around with pan keys + mouselook, scrollwheel for altitude. Selections and orders still work with the crosshair. Use your set toggle button, or open any menu, to switch to pointer. Press again or close the open menu to return to freelook.
LanguageData.M3AT_FreecamKeys: Set keyboard keys in RimWorld's keybindings. Current settings:
LanguageData.M3AT_FreecamButtonTip: A mouse-button version of the "toggle pointer" key above: it frees the pointer or goes back to looking. Default: middle button
LanguageData.M3AT_FreecamClickOffLooks: Freecam: empty left click closes pointer mode
LanguageData.M3AT_FreecamClickOffLooksTip: In pointer mode, a left click that selects nothing goes back to looking. Off (default): it only clears the selection, as in the game.
LanguageData.M3AT_FreecamPointerBackTip: Where the cursor appears when it is freed (pointer mode, an orders menu, a dialog or a tab). Last position: back where it was when looking began, an orders menu opening there with it. The crosshair: in the middle of the screen (default).
LanguageData.M3AT_FreecamPointerDotTip: While looking around, a small dot marks where the cursor will appear when it is freed (only with "Last position" above). Default: on
LanguageData.M3AT_FreecamMenuFreesPointerTip: How an orders menu opened while looking is used. Pointer select: the menu frees the pointer to pick from it, going back to looking once it closes (default). Crosshair select: the menu is pinned where it opened and you pick by turning the view onto an option.
LanguageData.M3AT_FreecamSnapArchitectTip: The pointer jumps to just right of the architect menu, on the map, when it opens, and goes back where it was if the menu is closed without picking anything from it. Default: off
LanguageData.M3AT_LookSpeedTip: How far the view turns for the mouse's movement, in degrees per pixel (default {0}).
LanguageData.M3AT_InvertMouseTip: Moving the mouse up looks down.
LanguageData.M3AT_FreecamCutawayTip: While flying, walls are cut down as IsoRim's own settings say: around the pointer (the middle of the screen while looking), near colonists and in front of rooms. Off (default): every wall stands at full height, as in IsoRim's first-person view.
LanguageData.M3AT_ScrollFlies: Scroll wheel flies up and down
LanguageData.M3AT_ScrollFliesTip: Scrolling up raises the camera and scrolling down lowers it, further at a higher flying speed. Off: the scroll wheel does nothing while flying.
LanguageData.M3AT_FlyingSpeedTip: How fast the camera flies, in cells a second (default {0}). Not affected by the game's speed.
LanguageData.M3AT_ScrollSpeedTip: How far one notch of the scroll wheel raises or lowers the camera, on top of the flying speed (default {0}).
LanguageData.M3AT_FieldOfViewTip: How wide the camera sees, in degrees from the top of the screen to the bottom (default {0}).
LanguageData.M3AT_GripToolButtonTip: Puts a toggle for the M3AT tools (weapon grip and clothing) among the small buttons at the bottom right of the map, beside the beauty and roof toggles.
LanguageData.M3AT_GripToolTip: Gives a colonist holding a weapon an "Adjust grip" button, to set where the hand holds that weapon and how it is angled, and anyone wearing clothes from another mod an "Adjust clothing" button, to pick which of M3AT's clothes they are drawn as. The same as the toggle at the bottom right of the map.
LanguageData.M3AT_GripClearAllConfirm: Forget the grips you set on {0} weapons? They go back to their usual hold.
LanguageData.M3AT_ToolsToggleTip: M3AT tools: show "Adjust grip" on colonists holding a weapon, and "Adjust clothing" on anyone wearing clothes from another mod.
LanguageData.M3AT_ClothesAdjustDesc: How M3AT draws this person: the content packs for its race or clothes, and each piece of clothing from other mods, drawn as the closest of M3AT's own or a content pack's. Pick a different one, or none, for any of them. Kept for that piece of clothing on everyone, in every game.
LanguageData.M3AT_ClothesNoPawn: Select someone wearing clothes from another mod.
LanguageData.M3AT_ClothesPaintTip: Paint the garment with this clothing's own sprites, as the "Paint stand-in clothes with their own art" option does. Untick it if the art comes out wrong on this one: it is then drawn in the garment's plain texture in the clothing's colour.
LanguageData.M3AT_ClothesHelp: Changes show at once, on everyone wearing that piece of clothing, in every game. "Add another" draws two together, such as a shirt and trousers for a one-piece suit. Clear them all in the mod options.
LanguageData.M3AT_ClothesClearAllConfirm: Forget the clothing choices you made for {0} pieces of clothing? They go back to being matched automatically.
LanguageData.M3AT_FaceNoPawn: Select someone with an animated face, and keep them on screen in the 3D view. Their face's mods are listed here.
LanguageData.M3AT_FaceMods: Currently tuning all faces from (click one to pick it):
LanguageData.M3AT_FaceCopyOthers: Copy these numbers to this face's other mods
LanguageData.M3AT_FaceRestoreDefaultsConfirm: Put every face mod's faces back where they are drawn by default?
LanguageData.M3AT_AdvancedTip: Click to show or hide tools most players won't need.
LanguageData.M3AT_FaceTuningIntro: Move and size the animated faces on the 3D head. Each mod that draws faces (Facial Animation, its retextures, a race's own faces) is set on its own, and kept for everyone with that mod's faces, in every game. Select a pawn, then open the tool: these options close so the face can be seen.
LanguageData.M3AT_FaceTuningNeedsGame: Face tuning opens while playing on a map.
LanguageData.M3AT_FaceHelp: Changes show at once on everyone using this mod's faces. The mouth moves on top of the whole face. M3AT fits other races' faces to the human layout by itself; once you tune a mod, it keeps the look you set even if that automatic fitting changes in an update. Back to automatic undoes your tuning for this mod.
LanguageData.M3AT_FaceTuneCleared: M3AT now fits {1} faces automatically, so your face tuning for {0} was reset. Tune it again in the face tool if it still needs it.
LanguageData.M3AT_FaceClearAllConfirm: Forget the face adjustments you made for {0} mods? Their faces go back to where they are drawn by default.
LanguageData.M3AT_GripAdjustDesc: Set where the hand holds this weapon and how it is angled. Kept for every weapon of this kind, in every game.
LanguageData.M3AT_GripNoWeapon: Select a colonist holding a weapon.
LanguageData.M3AT_GripNotSeen: The hands can't be shown for this weapon.
LanguageData.M3AT_GripStateAuto: Usual grip. Click or drag on the weapon to set your own.
LanguageData.M3AT_GripHelp: Changes show at once on the colonist (drafted, so it holds the weapon). They are kept for every weapon of this kind in every game, and can be cleared in the mod options. A positive angle tips the weapon's front up. The other hand reaches as far as the arm allows, and lets go while it is busy (reloading, a shield, a blow).
LanguageData.M3AT_GripOffOwn: Where you set the other hand.
LanguageData.M3AT_GripOffAuto: Other hand: where its stance puts it. Pick "Other hand" and click to set it.
LanguageData.M3AT_GripOffSeen: Where the other hand is now.
LanguageData.M3AT_GripSeenStance: Where the hand goes when drafted.
LanguageData.M3AT_GripOffSeenStance: Where the other hand goes when drafted.
LanguageData.M3AT_PowerArmourBulk: Power armour makes the wearer bigger
LanguageData.M3AT_PowerArmourBulkTip: A pawn in power armour (Spacer-tech armour over the body, arms and legs, such as marine, cataphract and recon armour) is drawn bigger and broader, with a smaller head for its size, as the armoured giant it is. Off by default, as the game's own armour is worn by ordinary people.
LanguageData.M3AT_ArmourBulkTip: How much bigger GrimWorld 40,000's Space Marine and Custodes armour draws its wearer. Default: {0} (a Space Marine of about 2.2 m to a person's 1.75).
LanguageData.M3AT_CompatibilityTip: Click to show or hide options for other mods' things.
LanguageData.M3AT_ArmourDrawScale: Armour drawn bigger makes the wearer bigger
LanguageData.M3AT_ArmourDrawScaleTip: Body armour another mod draws scaled up when worn (such as GrimWorld 40,000's Custodes armour, 110%) draws its wearer that much bigger.
LanguageData.M3AT_MarineBulkTip: A pawn in GrimWorld 40,000's Space Marine or Custodes power armour is drawn bigger and broader, with a smaller head for its size, by the armoured size under Pawns. GrimWorld's Marines are ordinary pawns made Marines by their armour, so it is the armour that makes them big. Scout armour, the Sisters of Silence and Malcador's robes are left as they are.
LanguageData.M3AT_SizeDesc: How big M3AT draws this pawn, against a grown pawn of the standard size, and how tall that is in map cells with the mod options' pawn height. This only changes how the pawn looks, not its body size in the game.
LanguageData.M3AT_SizeStandard: Grown pawn of the standard size: {0} cells
LanguageData.M3AT_PolyAboutTip: Why the poly counts shown here matter, and what is light or heavy.
LanguageData.M3AT_PolyAboutBodyChanged: The body in use has been changed by {0}: {1} polys.
LanguageData.M3AT_BodyCopy: M3AT is running from {0}'s own copy of it, so the body and garments drawn are that mod's and may differ from M3AT's.
LanguageData.M3AT_BodyCopyChanged: M3AT is running from {0}'s own copy of it, whose body has been changed: {1} polys (M3AT's: {2}).
LanguageData.M3AT_ContentButton: M3AT button on the bottom bar
LanguageData.M3AT_ContentButtonTip: Shows an M3AT button on the bottom bar in game while content packs are active, which opens the Content tab's list of packs over the map.
LanguageData.M3AT_ContentNotLoaded: Content packs are found once M3AT's figures have loaded: open a game in the 3D view first.
LanguageData.M3AT_ContentNone: No content packs are active. A content pack is a mod that gives M3AT's figures their own parts or clothes; modders can see Docs/RacePacks.md in M3AT's folder.
LanguageData.M3AT_ContentCompatLine: Content packs (mods with their own parts or clothes for M3AT): see the Content tab at the top.
LanguageData.M3AT_NoticeText: M3AT has a content manager for mods that add content to its 3D figures. In it you can choose, part by part, which content is drawn.\n\nThe content manager opens from the M3AT button on the bottom bar or the Content tab of M3AT's options.
LanguageData.M3AT_ContentCellPackTip: Draw the pack's for this part.
LanguageData.M3AT_ContentCellM3ATTip: Draw M3AT's own for this part.
LanguageData.M3AT_ContentEveryPartTip: Sets every part of this pack at once. On when every part is drawn from that side, neither while they are mixed.
LanguageData.M3AT_ContentAllPackTip: Draw the pack's for every part of this pack.
LanguageData.M3AT_ContentAllM3ATTip: Draw M3AT's own for every part of this pack.
LanguageData.M3AT_PartTip_Face: The face. M3AT's is Facial Animation's, fitted to the figure; a race with no Facial Animation faces has none.
LanguageData.M3AT_PartTip_Hair: The hair. M3AT builds it from the race's hair pictures.
LanguageData.M3AT_PartTip_HeadwearFit: How hats and helmets sit over the hair and ears.
LanguageData.M3AT_PartTip_BodyShape: Changes to the figure's body shape for the race.
LanguageData.M3AT_PartTip_SkinColour: The skin colour. M3AT's follows the colour the game shows for the race.
LanguageData.M3AT_PartTip_Clothing: The pack's garments for its clothing, or M3AT's closest garments painted with the clothing's art. Items opens the list, to choose for each piece.
LanguageData.M3AT_PartTip_GeneParts: The race's ears and tail, and parts drawn for genes (ears, tails, horns, scales and the like). M3AT's own are its models where it has them (a few popular races, cat ears, tails and horns), and elsewhere stand-ins built from the race's pictures. The pack's: on the pack's races only the pack's are drawn, and elsewhere its gene parts take the place of M3AT's.
LanguageData.M3AT_PartTip_Poses: Poses and animations the pack adds.
LanguageData.M3AT_PartTip_Other: Other changes the pack makes to how M3AT draws.
LanguageData.M3AT_HintNoFace: Facial Animation has no face for this race, so it is drawn without one. Download a Facial Animation face pack for this race (for example from the Steam Workshop) to give it a face.
LanguageData.M3AT_HintBuiltEars: M3AT builds them from the race's pictures. An early prototype: rougher than M3AT's other automatic parts.
LanguageData.M3AT_HintArmour: M3AT's own armour and helmets. The first packs' helmets covered the face.
LanguageData.M3AT_HintMatchedArmour: M3AT has no models of its own for some of this pack's armour and helmets: each is drawn as the closest match among M3AT's garments.
LanguageData.M3AT_HintModelEars: M3AT's own models of this race's ears and tail.
LanguageData.M3AT_HintMatchedClothes: M3AT has no models of its own for this pack's clothes: each is drawn as the closest match among M3AT's garments.
LanguageData.M3AT_HintFace: Facial Animation has faces for this race, fitted to the figure.
LanguageData.M3AT_HintHair: M3AT builds the hair from the race's hair pictures.
LanguageData.M3AT_HintHeadwearFit: M3AT's own fit of hats and helmets over the hair and ears.
LanguageData.M3AT_HintSkinColour: M3AT's follows the colour the game shows for the race.
LanguageData.M3AT_PartPolysTip: The pack's {0} pieces for this part average {1} polys each. M3AT's budget for them averages {2}: green is well within it, amber within it, red over.
LanguageData.M3AT_PartPolysCutTip: The pack's {0} pieces for this part average {1} polys each as drawn, auto-optimized from {2} as made. M3AT's budget for them averages {3}: green is well within it, amber within it, red over.
LanguageData.M3AT_ColMadeTip: The pack's pieces for each part, their average polys. Where M3AT had to cut them down (Auto Optimization), the first figure is what the pack made them with (red if that was over M3AT's budget, grey if not) and the coloured one, after the arrow, what M3AT draws. Green is well within M3AT's budget, amber within it, red over.
LanguageData.M3AT_ColPolysTip: M3AT's own for the same part, their average polys: the garments M3AT draws for the pack's items, or its models of the race's ears and tail.
LanguageData.M3AT_OursPolysTip: For the pack's {0} items M3AT draws its own garment or the closest match: {1} polys on average.
LanguageData.M3AT_OursPartsTip: M3AT's own models of the race's ears and tail ({0}): {1} polys on average.
LanguageData.M3AT_OursBuiltTip: M3AT builds these from the race's pictures the first time one is drawn, cutting each down to about {0} polys (an ear, tuft or horn) or {1} (a tail): shown is their mean.
LanguageData.M3AT_ContentUnfold: Show the pack's details: what it changes, its costs in full, and Measure now.
LanguageData.M3AT_ItemCellPackTip: Draw the pack's own garment for this item.
LanguageData.M3AT_ItemCellM3ATTip: Draw M3AT's automatic match for this item: {0}.
LanguageData.M3AT_ItemCellCustomTip: Pick any of M3AT's garment models for this item, or none.
LanguageData.M3AT_ItemCellCustomOnTip: Drawn as {0}, your pick. Click to pick another.
LanguageData.M3AT_ItemsAllPackTip: Every item below drawn as the pack's own garment (custom picks too).
LanguageData.M3AT_ItemsAllM3ATTip: Every item below drawn as M3AT's automatic match (custom picks too).
LanguageData.M3AT_PackPaintTip: Paint the pack's garment with this clothing's own sprites, as the game colours them, keeping the garment's shape. For a garment whose colours come out wrong.
LanguageData.M3AT_GarmentDetailTip:
Each garment from another mod is held to a budget based on M3AT's own garment for the same thing (or the one M3AT would draw for it: a one-piece suit is M3AT's shirt and trousers), and optimized as it loads if it is over. Images larger than {4} pixels a side are shrunk. Every poly is drawn for every pawn wearing it each frame.

High: up to {1} times M3AT's, cutting the most, for slower computers.
Default: up to {0} times M3AT's.
Low: up to {2} times M3AT's, keeping more of their makers' detail.
None: kept as their makers made them, up to {5} polys and twice the image size.

At Default, no garment is held under {3} polys. Optimized this session: {6}; the content switcher and the bug report name them. Takes effect after a restart.
LanguageData.M3AT_ContentPatches: Changes {0} of M3AT's own methods, some of which run every frame. A pack using M3AT's API needs none.
LanguageData.M3AT_HintOther: Changes M3AT's code in ways M3AT can't name; switching to M3AT's takes those changes off.
LanguageData.M3AT_GarmentDetailBody: <color=#ff8080>{0} changes M3AT's body: the body {1} polys, now {2}; M3AT's own garments {3}, now {4}. M3AT can't auto-optimize those at any level: this option lightens only other mods' own garments. Choose M3AT's body in the content switcher to undo it.</color>
LanguageData.M3AT_CostTrisTip:
Every poly of a garment is drawn for every person wearing it, every frame, so lighter garments mean a smoother game with more colonists.

For scale, M3AT's own: its whole body {0} polys, a shirt {1}, power armour {2}. A garment from another mod may have {3} times as many as M3AT's own garment for the same thing: {4} for this one. Over it, M3AT optimizes the garment as it loads.

Green: light. Amber: within the budget. Red: over it.
LanguageData.M3AT_CostTextureCut: Its image was {0} pixels a side, shrunk to {1} (the budget is {2}).
LanguageData.M3AT_CostColony: Colony poly count: {0} polys for {1} people, {2} each.
LanguageData.M3AT_CostColonyTip: Body and clothes, as drawn. M3AT's body with a full outfit of its own garments comes to about {0}; over {1} a person starts to cost noticeably with many people on screen.
LanguageData.M3AT_CostPack: {0} garments, {1} polys on average as made; {2} optimized, {3} images shrunk
LanguageData.M3AT_CostPackOver: ; {0} over budget kept as made (Auto Optimization: None)
LanguageData.M3AT_CostPackTip: Each garment against its budget: {0} times M3AT's own garment for the same thing (at least {1} polys), images of {2} pixels a side. Red means some of the pack's garments were over it.
LanguageData.M3AT_CostMeasured: Measured: {0} ms a frame (±{1}) with {2} people drawn, {3}.
LanguageData.M3AT_CostMeasuredSmall: Measured: too small to tell (±{0} ms) with {1} people drawn, {2}.
LanguageData.M3AT_CostMeasureNowTip: Opens M3AT's benchmark, which measures each content pack's cost apart from M3AT's. Have some people wearing the pack's content in view.
LanguageData.M3AT_HintBodyMeshPack: Reshapes M3AT's body and every garment for every person, of every race: several times the polys. Takes effect after a restart.
LanguageData.M3AT_BodyChoiceTip: Some content packs reshape M3AT's body and every garment as they load. That body is then drawn for every pawn of every race, so only one can be chosen.
LanguageData.M3AT_BodyChoiceNote: Currently affects every pawn. Restart required.
LanguageData.M3AT_BodyOverride: Currently overrides the body and every garment for every pawn! Poly counts:
LanguageData.M3AT_BodyOverrideAtRestart: Will override the body and every garment for every pawn! It is enabled when you restart the game, as the body is read once as the game loads; the poly counts show then.
LanguageData.M3AT_BodyOverrideNoAuto: This will also break M3AT's auto-optimization as it doesn't use the body API.
LanguageData.M3AT_BodyPendingRestart: The pack's body stays loaded until you restart the game.
LanguageData.M3AT_BodyChosenAbove: Body: {0}, chosen under Body at the top.
LanguageData.M3AT_BodyOneOnly: Only one content pack may change M3AT's body at a time, as two would stack on each other: {0}'s kept, {1}'s turned back to M3AT's. Takes effect after a restart.
LanguageData.M3AT_CostLoadTip: Time spent reading, optimizing and fitting this pack's garments to M3AT's body as the figures load (all of loading took {0} s). Optimized garments are kept on disk, so the next load is faster; garments within the budget load fastest.
LanguageData.M3AT_ContentSlowLoad: Content packs added {0} s to loading M3AT's figures: {1}. The M3AT button on the bottom bar shows what each costs.
LanguageData.M3AT_ContentLoadFresh: {0} garments fitted and kept, so the next load is faster
LanguageData.M3AT_ContentLoadSome: {0} garments fitted and kept, {1} from before
LanguageData.M3AT_PartTip_Armour: The pack's garments for armour and helmets (apparel named armour or a helmet, or in the game's armour categories). They have a row of their own because M3AT's armour and helmets came out better than the first packs' (their helmets covered the face). Items in the Clothing row's list can still be chosen one by one.
LanguageData.M3AT_RaceColDrawnTip: Whether the race is drawn as an M3AT figure at all.
LanguageData.M3AT_RaceColPartsTip: The race's own body parts: M3AT's models of them, or built from the race's pictures.
LanguageData.M3AT_RaceColFaceTip: Whether Facial Animation (or a face mod for it) has faces for the race.
LanguageData.M3AT_RaceColClothesTip: Clothing the race's mod adds: M3AT's own garments for it, or the closest of M3AT's garments painted with its art.
LanguageData.M3AT_RaceColStatusTip: How well the race's mod is supported, from M3AT's compatibility list (Docs/Compatibility.md in M3AT's folder).
LanguageData.M3AT_RacePackedTip: Also covered by a content pack: {0}. The notes here are what M3AT itself draws, for each part you set to M3AT's in the pack's row above.
LanguageData.M3AT_RaceChibiTip: Drawn as an M3AT figure, by the "Other races as 3D pawns" option.
LanguageData.M3AT_RaceChibiIsoPackTip: {0} (an IsoRim pack) makes this race 3D, so M3AT draws it as one of its figures.
LanguageData.M3AT_RaceCardPaperTip: Kept a flat card by IsoRim's "Keep as paper" list. To draw it in 3D, take it off that list: Mod options → IsoRim → Creatures and effects → Keep as paper.
LanguageData.M3AT_RaceCardIsoPackTip: {0} (an IsoRim pack) keeps this race a flat card. That is the pack's own setting, not M3AT's: check the pack's description or options.
LanguageData.M3AT_RaceCardOptionTip: M3AT's "Other races as 3D pawns" option is off, so races other than human stay flat cards. To turn it on: Mod options → M3AT: Maru's 3D Animated Toons → Mod compatibility → Other races as 3D pawns.
LanguageData.M3AT_RacePartsNoneTip: No ears, tail, horns or wings found among the race's parts: nothing to build.
LanguageData.M3AT_RacePartsOffTip: M3AT's "Race parts from their pictures" option is off, so the race's ears, tails and the like aren't drawn.
LanguageData.M3AT_RaceClothesNoneTip: The race's mod adds no clothing.
LanguageData.M3AT_RaceClothesOwnTip: M3AT has its own garments for all {0} of the mod's clothing.
LanguageData.M3AT_RaceClothesMatchedTip: {0} of the mod's {1} pieces of clothing have no M3AT garment of their own: each is drawn as the closest of M3AT's garments, painted with its art.
LanguageData.M3AT_RaceUntestedTip: Not on M3AT's compatibility list: it gets M3AT's general support for any race, and may look off.
LanguageData.M3AT_HintTunedParts: Drawn as M3AT's own parts, matched by hand to their pictures, so they move like M3AT's gene ears and tails:\n{0}
LanguageData.M3AT_HintTunedClothes: M3AT has no models of its own for this pack's clothes: each is drawn as the closest match among M3AT's garments, painted with its art, and for some of them M3AT's garments were picked by hand.
LanguageData.M3AT_HintTunedArmour: M3AT has no models of its own for some of this pack's armour and helmets: each is drawn as the closest match among M3AT's garments, and for some of them M3AT's garments were picked by hand.
LanguageData.M3AT_RaceClothesTunedTip: {0} of the mod's {1} pieces of clothing have no M3AT garment of their own: each is drawn as the closest of M3AT's garments, painted with its art. For {2} of them M3AT's garments were picked by hand.
LanguageData.M3AT_ModRowTip: {0}: adds no race of its own. M3AT has tuned matches for its genes or clothing.
LanguageData.M3AT_ModDrawnTip: Its people are humans (its own xenotypes), drawn as M3AT figures.
LanguageData.M3AT_ModNoRaceTip: Adds no race of its own.
LanguageData.M3AT_ModFaceTip: Its people are humans, with Facial Animation's human faces.
LanguageData.M3AT_ModPartsNoneTip: No ear or tail genes M3AT draws.
